name: Helpfulness (LLM-judged)
description: 10 everyday requests graded 1-10 by a judge model you choose, using reference notes.

items.input: Explain the difference between a list and a tuple in Python.
items.target: Lists are mutable and use []; tuples are immutable and use (). Tuples are hashable (usable as dict keys) when their items are. Mentions when to use each.

items.input: How can I improve my sleep quality? Give practical tips.
items.target: Consistent sleep schedule; limit caffeine and screens before bed; dark, quiet, cool room; regular exercise; avoid heavy late meals; see a doctor if problems persist.

items.input: Write a polite email asking my manager for a day off next Friday.
items.target: Has a subject line, polite and concise tone, states the date, offers to hand over or finish urgent work, thanks the manager.

items.input: What is the difference between RAM and storage?
items.target: RAM is fast, volatile working memory for running programs; storage (SSD/HDD) is slower, larger and keeps data when powered off.

items.input: Explain recursion to a beginner with a simple example.
items.target: A function that calls itself; needs a base case to stop; a correct small example such as factorial or countdown; warns about infinite recursion.

items.input: I have chicken, rice, onions and tomatoes. Suggest a simple dinner recipe.
items.target: Uses mainly those ingredients plus basic pantry items; clear numbered steps; rough quantities and cooking times.

items.input: What are the pros and cons of remote work?
items.target: Balanced: pros such as flexibility and no commute; cons such as isolation, communication friction and blurred work-life boundaries.

items.input: Explain what an API is using an everyday analogy.
items.target: An interface that lets programs request services from each other; a clear analogy such as a restaurant waiter; mentions requests and responses.

items.input: How do I calculate compound interest? Include the formula and an example.
items.target: Gives A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt) with each term explained and a worked example whose arithmetic is correct.

items.input: Give me a 3-day beginner workout plan.
items.target: Three distinct days with exercises, sets and reps suitable for beginners; warm-up; rest days; safety advice.
